instruction: I need you to add a new layer to this file and title it 'Oval'.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new layer in GIMP and naming it 'Oval'. The evaluator checks the GIMP config file to verify the layer-new-name is set to 'Oval'.
metadata.verification: Uses existing check_config_status metric with layer name 'Oval'.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic verification failure: The evaluator checks the 'layer-new-name' config setting, which is the DEFAULT name template for FUTURE new layers, NOT whether a layer named 'Oval' actually exists in the current file
Wrong state being verified: The instruction requires adding a layer named 'Oval' to the document, but the evaluator checks GIMP preferences instead of the actual document layer stack
Incomplete coverage: Neither requirement is properly verified - (1) 'add a new layer' is not checked, (2) 'title it Oval' only checks if config default is 'Oval', not if a layer with that name exists
Logic flaw: check_config_status at gimp.py:517 reads the gimprc config file (GIMP preferences), not the .xcf file structure (actual layers)
The config setting 'layer-new-name' = 'Oval' means the next layer created will default to 'Oval', not that a layer named 'Oval' currently exists
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Create a getter that parses the .xcf file to extract the layer stack (e.g., using GIMP's Python-Fu API or parsing the XCF file format)
Create a metric that checks if a layer with name 'Oval' exists in the layer list
Remove the Ctrl+Q postconfig or ensure the file is saved before closing, so the layer persists
Alternative: Use GIMP's scripting interface to query the layer stack instead of checking config files
